decisions.proposedPhrase: One tiny brake tap can create a traffic jam.
decisions.reason: Use the exact conditional-growth claim. A possible small perturbation is not an experimentally established particular brake tap or guaranteed trigger.

decisions.proposedPhrase: A traffic jam can appear from nothing.
decisions.reason: No obstruction is not no mechanism or cause.
Blame and a sole-cause explanation are unjustified; responses can amplify under some conditions.

decisions.proposedPhrase: Reaction time causes phantom traffic jams.
decisions.reason: Delay is one influence; finite acceleration, anticipation and following behavior also affect stability.
A slow/stopped congestion pattern can travel upstream relative to the road. Not all queue boundaries behave identically.
No unique initiator identified does not establish an absence of causes or human contributions.
Some stop-and-go patterns and queue boundaries propagate as waves. A jam is not universally one spontaneously generated backward wave.
